name: Ishvah
overview: Ishvah was a male member of the tribe of Asher, known specifically as a son of Asher. He is mentioned in the biblical record as one of the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, highlighting his place within the family of Jacob during a pivotal moment in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishvah means 'he will level,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may imply a sense of establishing or making level.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ishvah as a son of Asher, establishing his direct paternal relationship. No additional family relationships beyond this are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ishvah's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who went down to Egypt, a foundational event that set the stage for the later development of the nation of Israel. As a son of Asher, Ishvah represents one of the tribal ancestors who contributed to the growth and preservation of God's covenant people during a time of transition and divine providence.
